---
title: "Mortgage Amortization"
subtitle: "Excel | Loan calculator and 360-payment schedule"
---

## Overview

I built an Excel model that takes a home price, down payment, interest rate, and loan term, and returns the monthly payment, the full amortization schedule, and the minimum salary a buyer would need to qualify.

## Inputs and outputs

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Home price | $500,000 |
| Down payment (20%) | $100,000 |
| Loan amount | $400,000 |
| Interest rate | 7.00% |
| Term | 30 years (360 payments) |
| Maximum payment-to-salary ratio | 40% |

| Output | Value |
|---|---|
| Monthly payment | $2,661.21 |
| Total of all payments | $958,035.59 |
| Total interest paid | $558,035.59 |
| Minimum monthly salary to qualify | $6,653.02 |
| Minimum annual salary to qualify | $79,836.30 |

The payment does not include insurance or property taxes.

## What the schedule shows

The schedule splits every payment into interest and principal and tracks the remaining balance.

| Payment | Interest | Principal | Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $2,333.33 | $327.88 | $399,672.12 |
| 180 (year 15) | $1,732.52 | $928.69 | $296,075.46 |
| 360 (final) | $15.43 | $2,645.78 | $0.00 |

Because interest is charged on the remaining balance, the first payment sends only about 12% toward principal, and after 15 years the borrower still owes about 74% of the loan.
